# @scope/spreadsheet

> A spreadsheet renderer for the file workspace: .xlsx, .csv and .tsv in a virtualized grid with sheet tabs, search, frozen panes and merged cells.

- API reference: https://docs.example.invalid/api/spreadsheet
- Install: `npm install @scope/spreadsheet @scope/react react react-dom`

## README sections

- Install
- Entry: `spreadsheetRenderer()` returns a renderer.
- Standalone use: `SpreadsheetViewer` shows one file without a tree or a provider.
- CSS: Import `@scope/react/styles.css` and `@scope/spreadsheet/styles.css` once each.
- Options: `engines.xlsx`: loads SheetJS so `.xls`, `.xlsb` and `.ods` open too, as in `{ xlsx: () => import('xlsx') }`.
- Vite: Set `worker: { format: 'es' }` (Vite 7 and 8): the reader worker is code-split, which Vite's default `iife` worker format rejects.

## Entry points

- `@scope/spreadsheet`
- `@scope/spreadsheet/styles.css` (stylesheet)

## Exports of `@scope/spreadsheet`

- `SHEET_PARTS`: Every element this package renders carries `data-fs-part="<part>"`; these are its part names, all with the `sheet-` prefix.
- `SPREADSHEET_MAX_BYTES`: The largest spreadsheet the renderer and the standalone `SpreadsheetViewer` open: 50 MiB.
- `SheetClassNames`: Extra class names per part of this package, merged after the part's own class.
- `SheetPart`: A part name of this package.
- `SpreadsheetRendererOptions`: Options of `spreadsheetRenderer` and `SpreadsheetViewer`.
- `SpreadsheetViewer`: Shows a spreadsheet without a `FileSystemProvider`, read and drawn like the registry entry (see `spreadsheetRenderer`).
- `SpreadsheetViewerProps`: Props of `SpreadsheetViewer`: the standalone viewer props, with this package's parts in `classNames`, and the renderer options (`engines`, `workerFactory`).
- `spreadsheetRenderer`: Creates the registry entry for spreadsheets up to 50 MiB: `.xlsx` and `.xlsm` (read by our own bounded reader in a worker), `.csv` and `.tsv` (papaparse, in the same worker), and `.xls`, `.xlsb` and `.ods` through an injected SheetJS (`engines.xlsx`).
